money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The currency is the Algerian Dinar (DZD). It's illegal to import or export DZD. To avoid risks, only change money at: an exchange bureau at international airports or large hotels commercial banks in major cities Hotels and some businesses in larger cities accept credit cards. ATMs are available in major cities and large international hotels. Most accept international credit cards.

laws.rule: Drug use, possession, and trafficking are illegal in Algeria, with severe penalties. Foreigners caught with drugs face long prison sentences and heavy fines. Trafficking may also attract the death penalty.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Alcohol consumption is legal in Algeria but only allowed in licensed hotels, restaurants, and bars. It's illegal to be under the influence of alcohol in a public place.
laws.heading: Alcohol

laws.rule: Same-sex relationships are illegal and same-sex marriage is not recognised.
laws.heading: LGBTQIA+ laws

laws.rule: Although capital punishment has not been applied for many years in Algeria, the death penalty may be imposed for a range of crimes, such as murder, terrorism and drug trafficking.
laws.heading: Death penalty

laws.rule: In Algeria, it's illegal to: take photos of sensitive sites or military or security personnel attempt to convert Muslims to another faith give out material that authorities perceive as trying to convert Muslims to another faith import or export Algerian currency.
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: Standards of dress and behaviour are conservative in Algeria. This is particularly the case: in rural and traditional areas near mosques, shrines, religious schools and colleges Take care not to offend. Avoid physical contact between men and women in public. If you're female, it is recommended to wear loose-fitting clothes that cover your arms and legs.
laws.heading: Dress and behaviour standards

laws.rule: The Islamic holy month of Ramadan is observed in Algeria. Respect religious and cultural customs and laws at this time. During Ramadan, eating, drinking, and smoking may be illegal in public during the day. If you're not fasting, avoid these activities around people who are. Seek local advice to avoid offence. Explore our Ramadan page to learn more, including dates for Ramadan. The normal work week in Algeria is Sunday to Thursday.
laws.heading: Religious festivals

laws.rule: To drive in Algeria, you must have both: a valid Australian driver's licence (digital driver's licences may not be accepted) an International Driving Permit (IDP)
laws.heading: Driving permit

filming.next: Partner with a licensed Algerian producer.

visa-preparation.entry_summary: A visa is needed and must be obtained in advance. For Australians, applications go to the Embassy of Algeria in Canberra. Only tourists arriving and departing by cruise ship can get visas on arrival.
visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Visa from the Embassy of Algeria in Canberra, applied for by post or in person with the paper forms.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Send the complete application to the Embassy in Canberra (two signed forms, two photos, passport, travel insurance, bank transfer receipt, prepaid return envelope) and allow for processing time and post.

steps.step: Download and complete two copies of the application form, each with an original signature; fax and email applications aren't accepted.
Pay the fee by bank transfer with the applicant's name as reference and include the receipt.
Send the application with the passport, photos, travel insurance, any documents for the visa type and a prepaid self-addressed special delivery envelope.
Cruise passengers arriving and departing by ship can get a visa on arrival.

documents: Two completed and signed application forms
Extra documents for the visa type
Yellow fever certificate if arriving from or transiting (over 12 hours) a risk country
